guide: Open Start and type your practice name and your targets in the yellow cells: wanted profit margin, overhead share, pay share, cash floor, owner draw and the months of expenses you want in cash.

Check Team and Services. An employed clinician is paid a salary, a contract (self-employed) clinician a share of each session, an associate (works under supervision) per session. The owner draws profit instead of a salary.

Fill Profit by Month with revenue, pay, rent and other expenses, then Cash Months with what really moved in the bank. Profit, margin, pay share, overhead share and the history rows fill in by themselves.
Log expenses on Expenses and set a yearly budget for each category. Budget by Category shows the budget to date, what was spent and a Within budget, Watch or Over budget status.
Enter service and clinician profit by month. Each service type gets a Grow, Fix or Drop verdict; open the Losing Service Fix tool for a weak one.

Use the 13-week Cash Flow Forecast to see the lowest week against your cash floor, and the Safe Owner Draw tool before you pay yourself. The tax set-aside is a planning figure: confirm the share with your adviser.

Hiring Scenarios and Room Options compare ways to grow: first-year profit, break-even month and payback. A new clinician can bill a third-party payer (an insurer, an employer scheme or a public body) only after a wait; plan the cash.
Check your own local rules on tax, employment and billing. The workbook gives sample wording and planning figures only.
Use the 18 decision tools: each ends with a verdict and a what-if table. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready messages.
Why a workbook: one flat price, no per-clinician fee, and your data stays with you in your own file. The workbook holds status and money figures only, never note content.
Read the Practice Profit Dashboard and Charts every month: margin, pay share, overhead, cash cover, the weakest service and the next tax date.

listing.title: Therapy Practice Finance Excel Template: Profit, Cash Flow Forecast, Budget, Owner Draw, Hiring and Room Business Case
listing.headline: Know your profit, protect your cash and plan growth in one Excel file
listing.description:
Run the money side of a small group practice in one Excel workbook. Built for talking therapists and counsellors: an owner-clinician, employed clinicians, contract (self-employed) clinicians, an associate who works under supervision and a front-desk coordinator.

Profit by Month works out revenue, costs, profit, margin, pay share and overhead share and compares each month with your own history. Service Profit by Month gives each service type a Grow, Fix or Drop verdict; Clinician Profit by Month shows profit per clinician. Cash Months, the 13-week Cash Flow Forecast and Bills Due show the lowest week against your cash floor; Tax Set-aside, Budget by Category, Room Costs, Hiring Scenarios, Room Options and the Next 12 Months Budget plan the year.

18 decision tools answer the questions owners ask with a verdict and a what-if table: practice health, profit and loss, profit per service and clinician, losing service fix, fee check, break-even sessions, cash cover, safe owner draw, tax set-aside, hiring and room business cases, budget against actual and a 12-month profit forecast. Print 12 sheets and 12 reports, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready messages.

This is part eight of the Therapy Private Practice suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, one flat price with no per-clinician fee, your data stays with you, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data. Tax figures are planning figures only: confirm them with your adviser and check your own local rules. The workbook holds money figures only, never session notes or diagnoses, and it does not promise results.

Dashboard with 30 live figures and 22 charts

Hello {owner_name}, the milestone "{milestone}" is due on {target_date}. Due check: {due_flag}. {company}

Hello {accountant_name}, the owner draw for the month starting {month} was {owner_draw}. Please record it. {company}
Hello {accountant_name}, the profit and loss for the month starting {month} shows revenue of {revenue} and profit of {profit}. Please check it before the close. {company}
Hello {accountant_name}, please confirm the tax set-aside for the month starting {month}: {set_aside}, due {due_date}. {company}
Hello {accountant_name}, we bought {item} for {cost} on {date}, to be used for {years_of_use} years. Please advise how to record it. {company}
Hello {coordinator_name}, please check expense {expense_id} of {amount} paid to {paid_to} on {date}. {company}
Hello {coordinator_name}, the {category} spend this year is {category_year}. Please check that every receipt is filed. {company}
Hello {coordinator_name}, please pay "{item}" of {amount} by {due_date}. {company}
Hello {supervisor_name}, please confirm the {category} costs booked this year; we are {variance} against the budget to date. {company}
Hello {landlord_name}, this is {company}. Our rooms were used for {use_share} of the open hours in the month starting {month}. Could we talk about the rent?
Hello {landlord_name}, our room costs for the month starting {month} were {total_cost}. Please send us the breakdown of rent, cleaning and utilities. {company}
Hello {landlord_name}, we are looking at "{option}" with an extra rent of {extra_rent} a month from {start_date}. Can we talk? {company}

documents.title: Monthly profit and loss statement
paragraphs: Profit and loss statement of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month {col:pnl.month}.

Revenue {col:pnl.revenue} (session revenue {col:pnl.session_revenue}, group revenue {col:pnl.group_revenue}, sublet income {col:pnl.sublet_income}, less write-offs {col:pnl.write_offs}) from {col:pnl.sessions} attended sessions.

Costs {col:pnl.costs}: clinician pay {col:pnl.clinician_pay}, staff pay {col:pnl.staff_pay}, rent {col:pnl.rent}, other expenses {col:pnl.other_expenses}. Profit {col:pnl.profit}, a margin of {col:pnl.margin} against a wanted margin of {set:profit_target}. Margin check: {col:pnl.margin_flag}.

Pay share of revenue {col:pnl.pay_share}, overhead share {col:pnl.overhead_share} ({col:pnl.ovh_flag}). Profit per attended session {col:pnl.profit_per_session}. Profit after the owner draw {col:pnl.kept}.
Year to this month: revenue {col:pnl.ytd_revenue}, profit {col:pnl.ytd_profit}. Average profit of the 3 months before: {col:pnl.profit_3m}.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice and check your own local rules.
